title: Leaving Chicago for New York; Fats at 19
summary: Johnson left Chicago at 19 or 20, met Fats Waller at 19 and wrote a song with him the next year.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Yeah, that I thought I would never meet -- you know, and I didn't know how to go about meeting the person, and lo and behold, you come from Chicago with your chops still wet, you know, and you go to New York, and well -- to tell you the truth, I would say that most of my life has been spent in New York, and not in Chicago, because I left there early.
Oh, I guess 19 years old or 20, something like that. Because I met Fats Waller when he was 19, he was only 19 when we met.

And Fats and I wrote a song the next year, I think, when I was 20 years old -- I can't remember the song, but it'll come to me. And from then on, we were friends, and I have an album of songs that Fats autographed to me, that says, 'To my very best friend'.
I know -- Julie was telling me
how much he adored you, and you were such opposites. You know, and you just really balanced each other out.
Now we're going to spend a lot of time talking about Fats, and we'll probably transcribe that from another tape that we have....
But I would like to get now -- because we have to reserve a lot of space there for him, because he was your all time favorite --
He was my big, fat friend.
